title: Correctness of the Work Tape Encoding
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine over Booleans, let $x$ be a Boolean input, let $W$ be a natural number, and let $x_b$ be a Boolean-valued function on natural numbers. Suppose the encoding is good for every time and address below $2^W$, every index $j$ up to $|x|+1$, and every check, with input-bit data supplied by $x_b$. If $t+1<2^W$, the encoding is correct at time $t$, $h$ is a work-tape index, and $d$ is an integer satisfying $|d|+t+1\le 2^W-1$, then the encoded symbol on tape $h$ at time $t+1$ and offset $d$ equals the symbol actually stored there in the machine's configuration after $t+1$ steps on input $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-tape Turing machine over Booleans
The encoding satisfies every check for all $t,a<2^W$ and $j\le |x|+1$
The encoding is correct at time $t$
caveat: The supplied definitions do not give informal meanings for the encoding, its goodness condition, or correctness; the statement describes their roles as expressed by the theorem.
